SMTO-CFG-0014 — SMTO couldn't tell which Gateway should be the main one

GUID: 1d9843bd-e560-4570-9f6d-28e50ce72a71
Slug: composer-gateway-mismatch
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: cfg

What happened

  • Your message's settings named two different Gateways (the computers SMTO runs commands on) as the main one. SMTO stopped before starting any work so nothing runs on the wrong computer.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Select the button above the message box that starts with Target: (or shows Multiple gateways). Select Controls first if you don't see it. Check which Gateways are selected. This shows the Gateways the message would use and which one is marked as main with ★.
  2. Select Make primary next to the Gateway that should lead the work, then send your message again. Choosing the main Gateway again makes every part of the message agree on one computer.
  3. If it still fails, reload the page so the message box loads this conversation's current settings, then check the target again and send. An out-of-date page can hold an older Gateway choice that no longer matches.

What success looks like

  • Your message is sent and a task starts on the Gateway you marked as main.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send it to the person who manages SMTO. Don't keep sending the same message without changing the target; it will be refused the same way.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • ComposerValues validation failed because gateway_selection.primary_gateway_id differs from gateway_id in the submitted composer values.

What this means

  • Composer gateway_id differs from gateway_selection.primary_gateway_id. Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.

Why this can happen

  • Composer gateway_id differs from gateway_selection.primary_gateway_id.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare both exact Gateway IDs and the validated selection set.

How to fix it

  • Make composer_values.gateway_id equal gateway_selection.primary_gateway_id, or send gateway_selection as null with a single gateway_id. Clients should derive both from one target selection before saving the composer profile or submitting a task.
  • Make the composer Gateway ID match the selection's primary Gateway.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Both primary selectors identify the same intended selected Gateway.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
